introduction.situation: Information science studies records as they are made, described, ordered, found, used and kept by people and institutions.
introduction.complication: The inherited groupings mix stages, repeat the same topics from different sources and include residual and heading-only items, so no one can tell which stage a topic belongs to.
introduction.question: How can every topic in information science be placed under exactly one stage in the life of a record?
introduction.answer: Information science is divided by the stage in the life of a record, from creation to keeping: creation and publication, description, arrangement, retrieval and use, and preservation and governance.

governing_thought: Information science is divided by the stage in the life of a record, from creation to keeping: creation and publication, description, arrangement, retrieval and use, and preservation and governance.

field_check.governing_thought: Information science is divided by the stage in the life of a record, from creation to keeping: creation and publication, description, arrangement, retrieval and use, and preservation and governance.
key_line: Creation and publication is the stage in which records come into being, are produced and are issued to their audiences.
Description is the stage in which a record is named, listed and indexed so that its content and subject are represented.
Arrangement is the stage in which described records are ordered into classes by classification systems, theory and control structures.
Retrieval and use is the stage in which arranged records are stored, searched for, found and used by their readers.
Preservation and governance is the final stage in which records are kept, protected and managed over the long term.
